title: A Harbor for the Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1919, Hazel Crane works as a seamstress in a Baltic port city's diplomatic tailor shop, secretly ferrying coded dispatches sewn into uniform linings for a republic collapsing under occupation. A stranger named Ivo Markun arrives with a letter in the handwriting of Elias Brandt, the code-master who officially drowned months ago, demanding she help him finish a final cipher transmission that could expose the occupation's stolen treasury. As the workshop is raided, allies turn informers, and Hazel learns Elias is alive but compromised, she must choose between the law that abandoned her and a justice that exists only in the seams of her work. The novel ends at the century's turn, with Hazel transmitting the final cipher from the burning workshop and slipping out to sea, the truth sewn into a coat that will outlive the republic itself.
about_author: Tamsin Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from interwar Europe before turning to fiction. She lives near a working harbor and writes about the quiet people who move history with their hands.

chapters.title: The Seamstress's Silence
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Establishes her double life in the tailor workshop: stitching uniforms by day, hiding coded dispatches in linings by night. She memorizes the code-master's rules and trusts no one. Emotional beat: disciplined loneliness, the comfort of routine on the edge of collapse.

chapters.title: A Letter in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A stranger, Ivo Markun, corners her after hours with a letter written in Elias Brandt's unmistakable hand — the code-master officially drowned in October. The letter references a cipher only Hazel could verify. Emotional beat: vertigo; her careful world cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Republic Owes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He explains the mission: a final cipher, sewn into a ceremonial uniform for a peace delegation, proving the occupation looted the republic's treasury. Hazel resists, citing the network's rules. Emotional beat: reluctant bargain struck between strangers.

chapters.title: Measurements of a Traitor
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She begins the uniform while quietly testing Ivo's story against her own records. A workshop colleague, Marta, notices her late hours. Emotional beat: creeping suspicion — of Ivo, of Marta, of herself.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback to Ivo and Elias's shared past in the resistance; the ledger of stolen funds and why Elias faked his death. Present-day Ivo conceals a piece of the truth. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: First Raid
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Occupation officers search the workshop without warning; Hazel hides the half-finished cipher lining inside a finished officer's coat. Marta covers for her — or so it seems. Emotional beat: terror metabolized into colder resolve.

chapters.title: The Delegation Arrives
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The doomed republic's last diplomats arrive for fitting, including an old contact, Minister Voss, who may recognize the cipher's existence. Hazel measures him, passing messages in pin-pricks. Emotional beat: grief for a dying nation dressed in ceremony.

chapters.title: Signals in the Stitching
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo decodes the first section Hazel has sewn and discovers Elias's cipher contains a second layer — a list of collaborators, names that could include people they trust. Emotional beat: the mission's purpose curdles into danger.

chapters.title: Marta's Question
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Marta confronts Hazel with what she's seen, forcing Hazel to decide: recruit her, deceive her, or silence her. Hazel chooses trust — a break in her own rules. Emotional beat: the first fragile warmth in a cold season.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Night
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo meets a smuggler to arrange escape routes and learns the occupation has a price on the code-master's head — and on whoever finishes his work. He spots a watcher he recognizes: a man from Elias's own cell. Emotional beat: paranoia closing like a net.

chapters.title: A Handwriting Examined
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel compares the letter to her archive of Elias's genuine dispatches and finds an unsettling inconsistency — the letter is old, written before his 'death.' Someone is executing Elias's plan without him. Emotional beat: betrayal reconfigured; the mission may be a trap.

chapters.title: The Informer's Coat
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta is pressured by an occupation officer who knows she covered for Hazel. She must decide where her loyalties lie as her brother's debts are leveraged against her. Emotional beat: fear and love at war; a terrible bargain forming.

chapters.title: Second Raid
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The workshop is raided again — this time targeted. Marta is taken for questioning. Hazel, hidden in the loft with the cipher uniform, listens to everything. Emotional beat: survivor's shame; the cost of trust.

chapters.title: The Man Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo tracks the watcher and finds Elias alive, half-broken, in a harbor hospice — a prisoner of the occupation, forced to design the very trap meant to catch his network. Emotional beat: pity and fury entwined; the plan's true shape revealed.

chapters.title: What Elias Asked
chapters.summary: Elias's POV (a single chapter). Elias, through Ivo, sends Hazel a message: finish the cipher, but alter the collaborator list — he was made to include false names to destroy the resistance. Emotional beat: a dying man's attempt to unmake his own coerced betrayal.

chapters.title: Cutting the False Thread
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel reworks the cipher lining under impossible time pressure as the delegation's departure nears, while Ivo arranges Elias's extraction. Marta returns, changed, her loyalty unproven. Emotional beat: exhausted craftsmanship as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Fitting
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The final fitting with Minister Voss; the uniform — and the evidence — must pass inspection. An occupation examiner nearly finds the altered lining; Marta intervenes at real risk to herself. Emotional beat: breath-held triumph, and Marta's redemption.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Quay
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The extraction of Elias goes wrong at the harbor; the collaborator-watcher sells them out. Elias is shot covering Ivo's escape; the ledger pages scatter. Emotional beat: sacrifice and rage; the mission now runs on grief.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. New Year's Eve. The occupation announces the workshop's closure. With hours left, Hazel and Ivo transmit the corrected cipher through the delegation's departing uniform and the harbor's wireless relay. Emotional beat: the climax — one seam, one signal, everything staked.

chapters.title: Fire at the Workshop
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The occupation burns the workshop as evidence of its own erasure; Hazel saves only the pattern book and the coat containing the treasury proof, walking out through the smoke as Marta covers her exit. Emotional beat: destruction as cover; loss transformed into escape.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Uniform
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the quay, Hazel and Ivo board the smuggler's boat with the coat. The delegation's uniform crosses the border; the cipher reaches foreign presses. Emotional beat: quiet vindication — justice delivered outside any court.

chapters.title: What the Needle Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue, spring 1920. In exile, Hazel reads news of the treasury scandal breaking and resignations abroad. She takes in stitching again, teaching a young refugee the code. Emotional beat: memory preserved in craft; the work continues, hand to hand.
